_notes: bagCapacityPerPlayer: each player's bag holds 100 weight units (matches the CSV's Weight column directly, no conversion needed).
minPlayers: the CSV does not label a player requirement. Confirmed by the user (in-game) that this room is called 'Crisp Gallery', not 'Second Exhibit' — floor renamed accordingly.

value: NOT in the CSV. Secondary loot values are randomized per scope-out in-game, so this field is intentionally left null — the app should keep collecting it as a per-run user input, keyed to itemId.

BAY (Delivery Truck Crate) is the one exception: its true value can't be known until it's actually taken during the heist, so the UI renders it as a checkbox instead of a number input, driven by valueType/fixedValue below — checked locks its value to fixedValue, unchecked excludes it entirely, even if also marked Buyer's Choice. fixedValue was $122,500 (the $105k-140k community range, averaged) until 2026-08-03, when the user reported the truck's real value running lower than that average in practice, dropping it to a deliberately pessimistic $110,000; on 2026-08-09 the user asked to go further and pin it to the floor of that same $105k-140k range ($105,000) for optimizer math, rather than just a below-average estimate — same rationale, taken to its logical end. Intentionally never surfaced as a dollar amount on index.html — see internal/model-notes.md.

scopeNote: reminder-only metadata (2026-08-03), currently only on BAY — rendered on index.html under the item's name whenever present. Warns that the item isn't guaranteed to be scoutable/present at all (the truck doesn't always spawn), distinct from requiresPreps above (which warns about needing a prep mission, not about the item's existence being conditional).

requiresPreps: reminder-only metadata (2026-07-26) for four items that need the Glass Cutter prep to actually be lootable in-game (0-A, 2-B, 2-C, 2-K). No eligibility gating or optimizer behavior is wired off this field yet — guide.html just warns if any of these end up packed. Full gating (a toggle, state.activePreps, excluding these from the optimizer when the prep isn't active) is deferred to a future 'specify your preps' system; see internal/model-notes.md's 'Glass cutter item gating' section for that design.

variants/variantLabel: optional cosmetic sub-type picker (2026-08-04), currently only on 2-H (Gemstone) — the gem that spawns in the Crisp Gallery varies per run, and the crew wants the guide to name it. Purely descriptive: the selection is NOT an eligibility, weight, value, or packing input, it just rides along in saved state and gets displayed next to the item name. Any catalog item can grow a `variants` array and get the same dropdown on index.html with no JS changes.

floorMaps / xPct / yPct (2026-07-31, First Floor + Vault tagged 2026-08-06, Second/Crisp Gallery tagged 2026-08-06): floorMaps is a floor-name-to-image-asset lookup, many-to-one — Second and Crisp Gallery both point at assets/floors/second.png, since they're the same physical level in-game (confirmed by the user: the shared image has a dashed-rectangle callout in the app's own --floor-crisp-gallery blue marking the Crisp Gallery room's boundary within the larger Level 2 layout, a deliberate exception to the 'landmark labels stay off the coded palette' rule below, since this label IS the floor identity, not a generic wayfinding aid). Floors with no entry, e.g. Loading Bay, have no map at all — render code should skip rather than error. xPct/yPct are per-item, percentage-based, top-left origin, position on whichever image the item's floor resolves to via floorMaps. Alarm Floor was the pilot (smallest floor, 3 items) to validate pin rendering/legibility before tagging the rest; every other mappable floor followed the same way, sourced from the user's living CSV. Rendering (map-view.html's renderFloorMaps()) treats every floor identically — no per-floor code, so each additional floor was pure data entry. Every floor with a physical layout worth showing is now tagged. Loading Bay is deliberately excluded from floorMaps entirely, not just untagged — it's a single item (BAY) with nothing to visually distinguish, so a map adds no value there; map-view.html instead renders a text-only callout card for it (see internal/requirements.md).

description: rudimentary 2-4 word tag (2026-07-31) added to help players unfamiliar with the heist recognize what they're grabbing — sourced from the user's living spreadsheet at internal/secondary-loot.csv (gitignored, not shipped) and merged in here by itemId on request. Rendered always-visible inline next to the item name on both index.html and guide.html — see internal/requirements.md for the disclosure-vs-inline UI decision.
